Latin word

collēcta

collēcta, collēctae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a contribution of money, a collection; a contribution (to a shared meal)

In this lexicon

  • collection

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.233; Vulg. 1 Cor. 16.1

  • contribution

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.233: collēctam ā convīvā exigere (Lewis & Short)

Notes

  1. 1collēcta: long e (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). From colligō, participle collēctus, long by Lachmann’s law, as lēctus. Ruling: Lachmann’s law: āctus, lēctus, frāctus.

Examples

  • quoniam conlēctam ā convīvā, Crasse, exigis, nōn committam ut, sī dēfūgerim, tibi causam aliquam recūsandī dem

    since you demand my share like a dinner guest’s, Crassus, I won’t back out and give you an excuse to refuse yoursCic. de Or. 2.233

    In the entry for collection

  • Dē collēctīs autem, quae fīunt in sānctōs

    Now concerning the collection for the saintsVulg. 1 Cor. 16.1

    In the entry for collection
